activities.title: Road words
activities.description: Eight words from the road songs and stories. Flip each card, mark the ones you know, and come back any time.

cards.definition: A way to measure distance. One mile is about 1,609 meters.
cards.example: We drove three hundred miles before the rain started.

cards.definition: The line where the land meets the sky.
cards.example: The horizon disappeared behind the hills.

cards.definition: To trust a person to help you.
cards.example: You can always count on your brother.

cards.definition: To feel sad about something you chose, and wish you chose something else.
cards.example: I don't regret learning to play the guitar.

cards.definition: To show the way to a place or to something that happens.
cards.example: That decision led him to a job abroad.

cards.definition: A longer road instead of the short one.
cards.example: We took the long way round to avoid the traffic.

cards.definition: To look at a place very carefully and write down what you see, to make a map.
cards.example: A team of engineers surveyed the valley in March.

cards.definition: To have none left of something you were using.
cards.example: We ran out of paper before the map was finished.

activities.title: Water words
activities.description: Four easy words from our easiest song. A great place to start!

cards.definition: To bend paper or cloth so one part is on top of the other.
cards.example: Fold the letter before you put it in the envelope.

cards.definition: To get bigger, like a river after rain.
cards.example: The river swells after the heavy rain.

cards.definition: When something is good to try.
cards.example: The exam was hard but it was worth a chance.

cards.definition: To come back, again and again.
cards.example: The rain always comes again in November.

activities.title: Market words
activities.description: Words about work, money and food. You will hear them in the market song and the coffee podcast.

cards.definition: A big box, often made of wood, to carry fruit and other things.
cards.example: The crate of apples weighs twenty kilos.

cards.definition: To put things on top of each other in a neat pile.
cards.example: They stack the empty crates by the door.
Money changes hands quickly at a busy market.

cards.definition: To get ripe and ready to pick.
cards.example: The cherries ripen slowly at high altitude.

cards.definition: Coffee that comes from one farm or one place, not a mix.
cards.example: This bag is a single-origin from Huila.

cards.definition: How much water is in the air.
cards.example: The humidity in the afternoon decides how they spread the beans.

activities.title: Reading quiz
activities.description: Six questions about the road songs and stories. See right away if you got it, and your score at the end.

questions.prompt: In “Counting the Miles”, what does the singer count from the passenger seat?
questions.explanation: The first line says: “Counting the miles from the passenger seat.”

questions.prompt: What does “the long way round” mean?

options.text: A longer route taken instead of a direct one.
A short cut that skips the difficult part.

questions.explanation: That is just what the word list says: a longer road instead of the short one.

questions.prompt: In “The Long Way Round”, what kind of sentence is “If you had asked me, I would have said no”?
questions.explanation: “If you had asked” + “I would have said” is the full third conditional.

questions.prompt: What does the little square next to “el paso de la abuela” mean on the map?

options.text: A name that the local people use for the place.
A measurement Nilo could not check.
A bridge that still had to be built.

questions.explanation: It is the map sign for a local name, the name people who live there use.

questions.prompt: Complete the lyric: “Every mile is a door I ___ opened”.
questions.explanation: The line is “Every mile is a door I haven't opened.”

questions.prompt: What is the big idea of “The Long Way Round”?

options.text: The easy road is always best.
Sometimes taking a different road is the right choice.
You should stay away from country roads.
Going fast matters more than where you go.

questions.explanation: The song turns the long road into the big idea of the chorus: the long way is the one you remember.

activities.title: Easy song quiz
activities.description: Four questions about “Paper Boats”. Level A1, no tricks. Listen, read the words, and answer.

questions.prompt: What do you do first in the song?
questions.explanation: The first line is “Fold the paper, fold it twice.”

questions.prompt: Complete: “Down the steps and down the ___”.
questions.explanation: The chorus says “Down the steps and down the rain.”

questions.prompt: What does “Little boats that come again” mean?

options.text: Boats that come back again and again.
Boats that come for the first time.

questions.explanation: “Come again” means to come back, and here it happens again and again.

questions.prompt: Which line tells us an idea, not just a picture?

options.text: Every child is worth a chance.
Fold the paper, fold it twice.
Take the page and fold it well.
Send it off where waters swell.

questions.explanation: The other lines paint pictures. This one tells us an idea.

activities.title: Market quiz
activities.description: Five questions about the market song and the coffee podcast. Use both to find the answers.

questions.prompt: Complete the lyric: “___ for a pound and I'll take the whole crate”.
questions.explanation: “Two for a pound and I'll take the whole crate”.

questions.prompt: Why do cold nights up in the mountains make coffee better?

options.text: The bean stays small and sweet.

questions.explanation: The cold makes the coffee ripen slowly, so the bean stays small and sweet.

questions.prompt: Why is hand-picking better than machine harvesting?

options.text: It is cheaper for the farm.
Machines take ripe and unripe cherries together.
It is faster in the dry season.

questions.explanation: A machine takes the ripe and green cherries together. A person picking by hand can choose.

questions.prompt: What happens if the sun is too strong while the beans dry?

options.text: The sticky coat on the bean is lost.

questions.explanation: “Too much sun and they bake.”

questions.prompt: What does “Money changes hands” mean?

options.text: That people shake hands to agree.

questions.explanation: It means someone paid, and the money went from one person to another.

activities.title: Fill in the blanks
activities.description: Five sentences with a missing word. Pick the right word. You can try again as many times as you like.

blanks.sentence: Fold the paper and ___ the hat on top.
The little boat ___ down the steps.
blanks.hint: One boat, so the verb ends in -s or -es.
“Every” goes with a verb for one.

blanks.sentence: The rain always ___ again in November.
She ___ the letter before she put it in the envelope.

activities.title: Fill in the blanks
activities.description: Practice third conditional and past tense sentences. Pick the right word for each one.

blanks.sentence: If you ___ asked me, I would have said no.
I ___ taken the road that everyone praised.
She was certain that she ___ left the book at home.
blanks.hint: Something that happened before another thing in the past.

blanks.sentence: That decision ___ him to a job abroad.

blanks.hint: The present simple of “to be” with “I”.

activities.title: Listening practice
activities.description: Four short audio clips. Listen, answer, and see how you did at the end.

question.prompt: According to the fragment, what is the third step of the method?

options.text: Read the lyrics with a finger under the line.
Follow the voice half a word behind.

question.explanation: The third step is to sing: “Third, sing. Badly… You are singing for timing.”

question.prompt: What does “Is it running?” mean in this context?
question.explanation: In the episode, it means “Is it moving again yet?”

question.prompt: What time does the last tram leave?

activities.title: Reading time
activities.description: Read two short texts and answer the questions. Each text has a word list for the hard words.

passage.title: The box under the bed
paragraphs: Elena wrote her first letter when she was seventeen, and she never sent it. She wrote almost every week for thirty years, and she kept them in a banana box under her bed. She wrote on the backs of the delivery calendars from the shop on the corner, because paper cost money and her mother kept the calendars to wrap things in.

In 1994 the letter said: “Mara, today a man came to the house to ask for my hand and I said no. I do not know why I said no. Write and tell me if that was foolish.” By the time she was ready to send it, six months had passed and the question had become strange.

By the year thirty she had filled two boxes. The first held the years when she still believed she would send them. The second held the years when sending them had become a way of talking about herself.

questions.prompt: Why did Elena write on the backs of the delivery calendars?

options.text: Because paper was expensive and her mother reused the calendars.
Because the shop only gave her calendars.
Because she liked the numbers at the top.
Because Mara had asked her to.

questions.explanation: “Paper cost money and her mother kept the calendars to wrap things in.”

questions.prompt: What happened to the 1994 letter?

options.text: Mara answered it the same week.
It was never sent, and six months later the question felt strange.
It was the first one she sent.

questions.explanation: “By the time she was ready to send it, six months had passed and the question had become strange.”

questions.prompt: What was the difference between the two boxes?

options.text: One held letters from her husband and the other from Mara.
The first held years when she still believed she would send them; the second held years when sending had become talking about herself.
One was in the bedroom and the other in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: The last paragraph tells us about these two times.

activities.title: Reading time
activities.description: Our shortest text. Read it slowly. Three questions about what happens and how it feels.

passage.title: Thursday
paragraphs: On Thursday night the air was so still that the dogs did not bark. Tomás woke because the house was cold in a new way, and because he heard a sound he had never heard before: a long, thin crack, like a plate breaking in another room.
He went to the window. The river was white. Not white the way clouds are white, but white the way metal is white, and it was making that sound all along its length, from the bridge to the bend.

In the afternoon Tomás took his father's old skates and walked down to the bank. The ice was covered in a thin layer of snow, and where his foot landed the snow went under and the ice made a deep green sound under it, like a door. He stepped out. The first step was frightening. The second was not.

questions.prompt: What was strange about Thursday night?

options.text: The dogs did not bark, and the river made a sound Tomás had never heard.
The house was warm and the river was dry all night.

questions.explanation: The first paragraph tells us about the still air, the quiet dogs and the strange crack.

questions.prompt: How does Tomás describe the white of the frozen river?

options.text: White like snow in the morning.

questions.explanation: “Not white the way clouds are white, but white the way metal is white.”

questions.prompt: What happened with the first step on the ice?

options.text: It was easy, and the second was frightening.
It was frightening, and the second was not.

questions.explanation: “He stepped out. The first step was frightening. The second was not.”
